method: Picks for judges and ballot questions, read only against the owner's parameters: the Fishback platform planks, his three questions (commitment to the country and this area, foreign ties, big money that could sway them) and real-world experience for judges. A pick is made when a plank clearly points one way; 'Lean' when it points but something pulls the other way; 'Your call' when the planks are silent or split evenly. Nothing here is a party or endorsement read.

why: It raises the homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and limits what local governments can spend property taxes on. That is the closest thing on the ballot to the platform's 'eliminate homestead property taxes, roll back local spending'.
Newcomers wait five years for the full exemption, which fits 'Florida homes for Floridians'.
against: Florida Realtors put in more than $18M to pass it (big money on the yes side).
Sheriffs, police and firefighter groups oppose it over budget cuts. Manatee's sheriff estimates $23M less in year one.

why: It takes the property tax off tractors and farm tools, which helps working farms stay in business instead of selling to developers. That fits 'protect farmland' in your land and data-center planks.
The cost is small: about $31M a year statewide, and no political money is behind it.
against: Critics say the biggest farms, with the most equipment, save the most.

why: The platform says nothing about the state's savings account. Saving more is fiscal restraint, but it locks away up to $750M a year that could go back to taxpayers.
It buys natural land and farmland development rights to stop overdevelopment and protect drinking water, which is the heart of 'slow growth, protect land and water'.
The money for it comes from conservation groups, not developers.
against: It adds about $48 a year on a $300,000 home, and the platform wants local spending rolled back.
A county audit found the 2020 program's money was mixed with other funds. The county says it is fixing that.

why: The ordinance and the map aren't published online, and no source says why it's on the ballot. Leaving it blank doesn't affect your other votes.
It takes away the mayor's tie-breaking vote on the council. None of your priorities speak to how city hall is organized.
It caps the mayor and council at three terms in a row. Long stays in office build the donor ties your 'big money that could sway them' question worries about.
against: Voters already can remove anyone at each election.

why: It gives a strip of public land to the owner of a $7.25M beachfront lot, and no payment to the city was reported. The platform wants Florida land kept for Floridians, not handed to big buyers.
against: The city calls it housekeeping: the alley is unused and isn't a beach path.

why: It adds $68 a year to every developed parcel to grow the district's payroll, and the platform wants local spending rolled back, not raised.
against: It pays for a shorter firefighter work week (56 to 42 hours) that the chief says protects firefighters' health.

why: Part of the 2024 majority that let Florida's 6-week abortion limit take effect.
Ruled that regulators hadn't justified an FPL rate hike and called the utility commission a 'black box', siding with customers over a big utility.
Seven years on the court, with a career as a government lawyer before that.
against: He had never been a judge before his appointment.
Reported in 2013 to have been part of the discussions that led to no action on the Trump University complaints.

why: Nothing found against your priorities. His career is real legal work: state agency general counsel and a court clerkship, plus Army service.
against: No notable rulings found either way.

against: No notable rulings found either way.
